conventions.convention: Matrix encodings use one fixed entry-approximation machine with a uniform polynomial bound in description length plus unary requested precision. Hermiticity and norm bounds concern exact matrices and are promises.

Local support factors are ordered by increasing qubit index. Terms may have empty support; n,m≥1. Locality k is fixed, local norms have a polynomial bound, and the threshold separation is inverse polynomial.

The verifier is generated from unary input length over the fixed QC14 alphabet. Its witness is arbitrary, its other input wires are initialized as specified, and acceptance uses a total polynomial-time terminal predicate, summing over all unmeasured wires.
Normalized Clifford–T representatives may be replaced by physical letters up to a scalar only for an unconditional block. A scalar inside a controlled block must be retained.
Parallel repetition accepts when S≥ceil(r(c+s)/2), copies only the classical basis input, and uses distinct witness, input and workspace registers for each verifier copy.
T≥1, N=T+1, legal unary time is c_t=1^t0^(T−t), acceptance is output bit 1, and the output rejection penalty has coefficient N. Propagation edges have weight 1/2.
For the geometric soundness bound, the input x is fixed and every initially unrestricted wire belongs to the witness; every other work wire is checked for zero initialization.
The KKR two-qubit restriction requires T2≥1, L≥5, T=(T2+1)L−1, and controlled-Z gates at times lL, with the specified surrounding Z gates.

load_bearing.statement: For Hermitian H1,H2, a nonzero subspace S on which H2 vanishes, and H2≥J on S⊥ with J>2||H1||, the least eigenvalue of H1+H2 lies between λ_S−||H1||²/(J−2||H1||) and λ_S, where λ_S is the least eigenvalue of the compression of H1 to S.

For fixed q and D=2^q, an effectively supplied D×D unitary can be synthesized within rational error η, up to one global scalar, using a constant number of exactly returned clean ancillas and polynomial bit cost and gate count in description length and 1/η.

For γ=c−s>0 and 0<δ<1, every integer r≥2γ^−2 ln(1/δ) gives completeness at least 1−δ and soundness at most δ for the parallel midpoint verifier, including soundness against every entangled r-block witness.

A fixed polynomial-time machine producing polynomially bounded QC14 circuit descriptions can be simulated by a full-list input-length-uniform QC14 family to inverse-polynomial operator error δ, up to global phase, with polynomial size and generator time; data outcome probabilities change by at most 2δ.

For fixed k, effectively encoded Hermitian K on at most k qubits and positive rational B≥||K||, a QC14 circuit approximates the effect E=(I−K/B)/2 within η, with polynomial cost in b+ℓ(η)+1/η; the ideal marked dilation has polynomial-time Cauchy names and its selector-controlled block can also be synthesized.

On legal clocks, propagation is unitarily conjugate to the half-weight path Laplacian tensored with computation identity; its kernel consists of valid histories and its first positive eigenvalue is 1−cos(π/(T+1))≥2/(T+1)².

For the specified input-specific NO verifier with soundness at most 1/8 and every nonwitness initial wire checked, every unit propagation history has squared projection onto ker(Hin+Hout) at most 1−1/(2N), and the legal-clock ground energy is at least 1/(2N³).

Under the stated padded controlled-Z circuit conditions, the compressed KKR propagation penalty dominates H′, the half-weight block path scaled by 1/L, whose kernel is correct propagation and whose gap is at least 2/[L(T2+1)²]. Choosing J2g2>2K2+K2²/ε2 gives restriction error below ε2.

For fixed locality and polynomial-time Cauchy entry encodings, rational Hermitian local approximations can be produced with total operator error at most τ. Ground energies change by at most τ; thresholds a+τ,b−τ preserve both promise sides and retain at least three quarters of the original gap when τ≤(b−a)/8.

concerns.concern: Statement pads the program to L(n) fixed-width gate records, but Proof 1.1 says 'For each output position i≤L(n)' and returns the 'ith bit of its padded record string', then concatenates L(n) Boolean circuits. A record has multiple bits, including wire addresses, so this construction computes only the first L(n) bits rather than the complete program. Indexing all bits of the polynomial-length padded string closes the proof gap.

The Definition calls A_n 'a clean-ancilla register' and repeatedly calls its initially zero wires 'clean ancillas', while citing def-qc-clean-and-dirty-ancillas. That supplier defines a clean ancilla by exact terminal return to zero for a declared target unitary; zero initialization alone is explicitly insufficient in def-qc-circuit-cost-model. The verifier interface supplies initialization but no return contract, and general verification need not restore those wires. The page summary repeats the terminology.

The Statement calls 4D_−,D_−,D_−,2D_+ the 'legal-clock matrix on the adjacent coordinates' c_(t−1),c_t. These are equivalent endpoint representatives only after compression to S_prop1, as the surrounding proof intends. They are not the principal matrices on the full legal-clock space: in physical sector 00, the displayed local terms give endpoint diagonal entries 1/8 and off-diagonal entries −2, whereas 4D_− has diagonal entries 2. Proof 1.1 similarly says the snapshot quadratic forms contribute endpoint diagonal entries 'in physical clock coordinates' without explicitly retaining the compression qualification. The distinction is explicit in the source's restriction argument: [KKR, §5, PDF pp. 12–15](https://arxiv.org/pdf/quant-ph/0406180).

Proof 1.1 says to 'pad each segment ... to length L' and then sets T=(T2+1)L−1 with controlled-Z gates at lL. Those times require L−1 one-qubit steps in each segment before, between, and after the controlled-Z gates. Padding the one-qubit segments to L steps instead gives controlled-Z times l(L+1) and total length (T2+1)L+T2. The intended L−1 padding is an immediate correction, but the written instructions do not produce the asserted schedule.

seams_checked.note: The consumer retains unary-length full-list generation, the fixed QC14 alphabet, terminal predicates, and separate classical costs. Input-dependent compilation is mediated by the explicit interpreter. The clean-ancilla terminology concern is recorded separately.
The opened Dirac conversion definition fixes first-argument-linear root pairings and ket-bra coordinate matrices; witness effects and history terms use the corresponding adjoints consistently.
Witnesses are positive trace-one operators on nonzero spaces. The pure-witness theorem derives a finite spectral ensemble directly and preserves the acceptance threshold.

POVM outcome weights use the finite trace law and normalization. The local-energy dilation is constructed explicitly; no conditional output state or free measurement implementation is inferred from a POVM.

Ordered tensor factors, one-dimensional zero-qubit registers, and contraction of discarded factors agree with the opened definitions and partial-trace characterization. Amplification multiplies embedded full-space effects and tensors only the one-block effects.
The consumer preserves the exact H,T phases and rotation signs. Its exact identities X=HT^4H, Z=T^4, and CNOT=(I⊗H)CZ(I⊗H) agree with the supplied matrices.

The normalized dense SU(2) package matches the opened density statement. Synthesis respects the compiler's rational tolerance domain and uses global-phase freedom only for unconditional factors; controlled blocks are synthesized as complete fixed-dimensional matrices.
